titulo: Hello, world!: Pronouns, «to be» and gender

aula.objetivo: Greet people in any situation, recognise 13 new letters, say what your name is and tell formal from informal.

blocos.titulo: Лена и фото / Lena and the photo
blocos.ru: Привет! Меня зовут Лена. Я студентка. Вот фото. Это Москва: вот школа, вот театр, вот музей, а там кино. Это мама, а это папа. Это брат Антон. Он студент. Это сестра Вера. Она тоже студентка. Вот дом. Я тоже тут! Пока!
blocos.pt: Hi! My name is Lena. I am a student. Here is a photo. This is Moscow: here the school, here the theatre, here the museum, and over there the cinema. This is the mother, and this is the father. This is the brother, Anton. He is a student. This is the sister, Vera. She is a student too. Here is the house. I am here too! Bye!

perguntas.pergunta: What is the girl's name? Answer in Russian.
Who is Anton? Answer in Russian.
Who is Vera? Answer in Russian.

blocos.titulo: Pronouns and the missing verb «to be»
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: Pronouns are short words, and you have already used three: «я» (yah), I; «ты» (ty), you (informal); and «вы» (vy), you (formal or plural). STEP 2: The others are «он» (ohn), he; «она» (ah-NAH), she; «оно» (ah-NOH), it, for neuter things; «мы» (my), we; and «они» (ah-NEE), they. STEP 3: Russian has no verb «to be» in the present tense. To say «I am a student», say only «Я студент» (yah stoo-DYENT). Literally: «I student». STEP 4: This applies to all pronouns: «Он студент», «Она студентка», «Мы тут», «Они там». No verb in the middle. STEP 5: In writing, between two nouns, a dash is sometimes put in place of the «is»: «Антон — студент». When speaking, make a small pause where the dash is. STEP 6: A man says «студент» and a woman says «студентка». With «Я», the next word shows the gender of the speaker.
blocos.comparacao: in English the verb changes with the person: «I am», «he is», «we are». In Russian, in the present tense, nothing changes and nothing appears: only the pronoun and the rest of the sentence.

exemplos.pt: I am a student. A man is speaking.
Are you a student? To a friend.

erros.motivo: In the present tense «есть» is not used in place of «is». The pronoun and the word are enough.
For a woman, the word changes: «студентка».

blocos.titulo: The gender of nouns: masculine, feminine and neuter
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: Every Russian noun has a gender: masculine, feminine or neuter. You find the gender by looking at the last letter. STEP 2: Ends in a consonant, or in «й»: masculine. Examples: «брат» (braht), «дом» (dohm), «город» (GOH-raht) and «музей» (moo-ZEY). STEP 3: Ends in «а»: feminine. Examples: «мама» (MAH-mah), «сестра» (sees-TRAH), «школа» (SHKOH-lah) and «жена» (zhee-NAH). STEP 4: Ends in «о»: neuter. Examples: «кино» (kee-NOH), «метро» (mee-TROH) and «фото» (FOH-tah). STEP 5: Careful: in English only people and some animals have a gender (he and she), while things are «it». In Russian every noun has one, so a thing can be «he» or «she»: «брат» is «он», «сестра» is «она», and «кино» is «оно». «Игра», game, is feminine in Russian. And «папа» is masculine, although it ends in «а», because he is a man. STEP 6: The gender chooses the pronoun: masculine is «он», feminine is «она» and neuter is «оно». That is why «брат» is «он», «сестра» is «она» and «кино» is «оно». You will see other endings in lessons 4 and 5.
blocos.comparacao: English has no articles that show gender, so you never had to think about it. Russian has no articles either: the ending of the word is what shows the gender.

exemplos.pt: This is the brother. He is a student.
This is the sister. She is a student.
This is the house. It is over there.
This is the school. It is over there.
This is the cinema. It is over there.
This is the photo. It is here.

erros.motivo: «Папа» ends in «а», but he is a man. That is why it is masculine and the pronoun is «он».
Words ending in «о» are neuter. The pronoun is «оно», not «она».

itens.explicacao: The last word has one syllable and ends in t: «брат». «друг» ends in k.
It starts with «Она» (ah-NAH) and ends with «студентка», with the final «ка» that marks a woman.
The pronoun is «Мы» (my), we, and the final word is «тут», here.
From lesson 1: the question starts with «Кто» (who). The other two start with «Как» (how).
Two words and no verb: «Я» and «студент». The speaker is a man.

itens.enunciado: Listen, repeat aloud and then show the answer.
itens.explicacao: Hi! I am Anton. And you?
No «is»: «Она» and then «студентка». The ending «-ка» shows that she is a woman.
With «Это», no verb. Write «папа» with two «п» and two «а», as in «мама».
It ends in «а», and words in «а» are feminine.
It ends in «о», and words in «о» are neuter. The pronoun is «оно».

itens.enunciado: Listen, repeat aloud and then show the answer.
itens.explicacao: Great! Are you a student?
It ends in a consonant («д»), and that is the typical masculine ending.
It ends in «а», but he is a man. It is an important exception: the pronoun is «он».
«сестра» ends in «а», it is feminine, and the feminine pronoun is «она».

itens.enunciado: How does a woman say «I am a student»?
itens.explicacao: There is no «есть» in the present tense, and the word for a woman is «студентка».

itens.enunciado: Which pronoun do you use to talk about yourself and a friend together?
itens.explicacao: «мы» is we. «они» is they and «вы» is formal you or you plural.

itens.enunciado: Listen, repeat aloud and then show the answer.
itens.explicacao: Hello! What is your name? (formal)
«брат» is masculine, so the pronoun is «Он».
«сестра» is feminine, so the pronoun is «Она».
«кино» is neuter, and the neuter pronoun is «оно».
The person answering is talking about themselves, so they use «я» (I).

itens.enunciado: Listen, repeat aloud and then show the answer.
itens.explicacao: Great, thank you. And you? (formal)
From lesson 1: the question «Кто это?» asks for a person, and «мама» is the answer.

itens.enunciado: Put in order: «I am a student.» (a man speaks)
itens.explicacao: No verb: the pronoun «Я» comes first and then the occupation.

itens.enunciado: Put in order: «We are over there.»
itens.explicacao: The pronoun comes first and then the place. There is no verb «to be».

itens.enunciado: Write in Russian: «Hi! My name is ... I am a student.» Use your own name.
itens.respostaEsperada: Привет! Меня зовут Лена. Я студентка.

itens.enunciado: Write in Cyrillic: «Good morning! What is your name?» (formal)

blocos.enunciado: Record yourself for 30 seconds: greet, say «Меня зовут …», say whether you are a student («Я студент» or «Я студентка»), introduce two people or photos («Это … Он … / Она …») and say goodbye.
blocos.exemplo: Здравствуйте! Меня зовут Лена. Я студентка. Это брат. Он студент. Пока!

blocos.enunciado: Write in Cyrillic: thank you, please, good morning, bye, goodbye.
